title: Final: the whole TileLoader
sub: Find every bug in the tile loader
cards/0/body:
Here is the whole tile loader. You have seen it in pieces: blocking, races, timers and cancellation. Now find everything yourself. There are more than ten bugs, and they are linked: one hides another.

A hint on the order: first scan the threads (who runs which line), then the shared data (who writes and who reads), then the lifetimes (who holds a reference, who will stop what).
cards/1/task: Find all bugs in TileLoader. Tap the problem lines, then press Check. There are 12 in total.
cards/1/bugs/0/title: Synchronous Wait() in an async method
cards/1/bugs/0/why: The GetOrAdd factory runs on the caller's thread. On the Unity main thread that means a freeze and a deadlock: Release sits in a continuation that Unity posts back to the same blocked thread. Use await _throttle.WaitAsync(ct).
cards/1/bugs/1/why: Any network or Parse error leaves the spot taken. After four errors the semaphore is exhausted for good, and _pending is not decremented, so _allLoaded never fires.
cards/1/bugs/2/why: It blocks a thread: the continuation after await came back to the Unity main thread, so the frame stalls. Use await Task.Delay(50, ct). The continuations should also leave the main thread via ConfigureAwait(false).
cards/1/bugs/3/title: The token is never used, and PreloadAll passes None
cards/1/bugs/3/why: GetByteArrayAsync is called without a token, and None disables cancellation entirely. Besides, the factory captures the first caller's token, so their cancellation hits everyone sharing the task.
cards/1/bugs/4/why: --_pending loses updates, and zero is possible between tiles, so "all loaded" fires too early. A second SetResult throws. Use Interlocked, TrySetResult and RunContinuationsAsynchronously.
cards/1/bugs/5/title: GetOrAdd starts LoadAsync in the factory
cards/1/bugs/5/why: The factory may run on two threads: the tile loads twice and the counter and semaphore are hit twice. Store a Lazy<Task<Tile>>.
cards/1/bugs/6/title: Failed tasks stay in the cache forever
cards/1/bugs/6/why: A repeated GetTileAsync returns the same failed or cancelled Task, with no retry. Failed entries must be removed.
cards/1/bugs/7/why: Other threads write to the Dictionary under a lock, while TryGetLoaded and ReportProgress read it without one. A read during a write yields garbage or an exception.
cards/1/bugs/8/why: Nothing references the timer: in .NET the GC collects it and progress quietly freezes; in Mono (Unity) it cannot be stopped. Also the callback runs on the pool and writes to the Slider, while Unity API is main-thread only.
cards/1/bugs/9/title: StartNew(async) and Delay without a token
cards/1/bugs/9/why: You get a Task<Task> and loop exceptions are lost. Task.Delay(1000) is not interrupted by Stop(). Use Task.Run and a token.
cards/1/bugs/10/why: A plain bool across threads formally does not guarantee the loop sees the write, and Stop() does not wait for the loop to end. Use a CancellationTokenSource.
cards/1/bugs/11/why: The tasks are discarded: errors are invisible and nobody can wait. And the factory with Wait() runs right in the loop: from the fifth id on, PreloadAll blocks the calling thread (on the main thread, a deadlock). Return a Task instead.
cards/2/q: When does the Wait() in LoadAsync cause a deadlock?
cards/2/options/0: GetTileAsync is called from the Unity main thread while all 4 spots are taken
cards/2/options/1: Only if the call comes from a thread-pool thread
cards/2/options/2: Only if the tile server is unreachable
cards/2/options/3: On any call, even when spots are free
cards/2/explain: Wait() has to really block (no free spots) and block the main thread that Unity will post the Release continuations to (which happens if the loads holding the spots also started on the main thread). While spots are free, Wait passes instantly.
cards/2/wrong/3: With a free spot Wait() returns at once; nothing blocks.
cards/3/q: Which changes in LoadAsync are actually needed?
cards/3/options/1: Release and the counter decrement in finally
cards/3/options/3: await Task.Delay(50, ct) instead of Thread.Sleep(50)
cards/3/explain: The lock around the dictionary write is fine here and short. A Mutex is heavier, thread-affine and fixes nothing. The other three changes remove the blocking and the lost spot.
cards/4/q: Replace the stop flag with a token: complete the background loop.
cards/4/explain: Task.Run unwraps the async lambda, and Cancel signals both the loop and the Delay. Task.Delay throws on cancellation, so in real code you catch OperationCanceledException.
cards/5/q: Put the correct LoadAsync outline in order.
cards/5/items/0: await _throttle.WaitAsync(ct): wait for a spot without blocking
cards/5/items/2: Download and parse the tile, passing ct
cards/5/items/3: Write the result into _loaded under a lock
cards/5/explain: Take the spot before the try (otherwise a cancelled wait would release a spot we never took) and give it back in finally in every case.
cards/6/q: Match each bug to its consequence.
cards/6/pairs/0/1: After four errors every load hangs
cards/6/pairs/1/0: The Timer callback writes to the Slider
cards/6/pairs/1/1: Unity API is called off the main thread
cards/6/pairs/2/1: Errors in the background loop are lost
cards/6/pairs/3/0: GetOrAdd starting work in the factory
cards/7/q: A player reports: after a few network failures the map stops loading even though the network is back, and the game does not lag. What is the most likely cause?
cards/7/options/0: The semaphore spot is not returned on error (no finally)
cards/7/options/1: The Timer was collected by the GC
cards/7/explain: The symptom "quietly stopped loading after errors, no lag" is an exhausted semaphore. A frozen main thread would show as lag, and a Timer problem would only affect the progress bar (and in Unity's Mono runtime an unreferenced timer is not even collected).
